requested.title: What If You Saw Who Wants You to Fail?
requested.description:
Say your good news out loud, and a card snaps open over the listener's head: how much your win hurts them. Six weeks before Korea's big exam, who is really racing you?

Be honest: what number would open over your head? Tell us in the comments. The best what-ifs become videos.

Chapters
0:00 Made the cut
1:11 The rule
2:39 Who's red
5:09 The weapon
6:28 A thousand cards
7:56 The ladder
8:46 Backs
10:31 The window

The card is made up. The facts are real:
- On Korea's college entrance exam, most subjects are graded on a curve, and the top grade goes to the top 4 per cent:
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_Scholastic_Ability_Test
  https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/education/20260806/korea-considers-using-ai-to-grade-csat-essay-answers
- On exam day in November 2025, planes stopped taking off and landing for 35 minutes during the English listening test: TRT World
  https://www.trtworld.com/article/f19ad18cc24f
- Seoul's cram schools may teach only until ten at night, and inspectors have patrolled the streets to enforce it: Korea JoongAng Daily; TIME (2011)
  https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/ordinance-to-extend-hagwon-hours-in-seoul-sparks-debate-over-regulating-cram-schools/12409013
  https://content.time.com/time/printout/0,8816,2094427,00.html
- Daechi-dong, in Seoul, has about a thousand after-school academies:
  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daechi-dong
  https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-10-24/south-korea-launches-happy-education-policy-to-shorten-study-ho/5840152
- In one brain-scan study, envying someone who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain: Takahashi et al., Science (2009)
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19213918/
- Envy comes in two kinds, benign (move up) and malicious (pull the other down): Van de Ven, Zeelenberg and Pieters, Emotion (2009)
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19485619/
- We compare ourselves with people close to our own level: Festinger (1954), A Theory of Social Comparison Processes
  https://www.humanscience.org/docs/Festinger%20(1954)%20A%20Theory%20of%20Social%20Comparison%20Processes.pdf
- We envy people who started out like us, in what matters to us, and people don't like to admit malicious envy, even to themselves: Van de Ven, Zeelenberg and Pieters, Motivation and Emotion (2012)
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3356518/

Narrated with an AI voice. Animated in code.
